name: Main Agent Prompt — Client Working Memory (split fields)
description:
Main-agent variant driven by the derived client working memory (docs/client-working-memory-design.md), with the memory exposed as one placeholder PER SECTION instead of a single opaque block. Same store, same consolidation call, same cost as the block form — the only difference is that a curator can read the prompt to see what is being fed, and can reorder, relocate or drop an individual section to experiment. Selecting this prompt is the entire opt-in; re-selecting another prompt is the whole rollback. Needs CLIENT_WORKING_MEMORY_ENABLED as well.

Do NOT also add {client_working_memory} to the body — a prompt declaring both forms renders the block and leaves these section headings bare.

Two things a reader should not mistake for omissions. {state_x_guidelines} is present and authored by you: the block form swallowed it, this form does not. {retrieved_context} is absent because it is blank in EVERY prompt fleet-wide — RETRIEVED_CONTEXT_DEFER_TO_SUFFIX delivers knowledge sources as a trailing message after the conversation history instead, so adding the placeholder back would render nothing and imply retrieval had broken. {character_profile_text} IS genuinely dropped: recalled backstory arrives a few facts at a time through 'What is on your mind from your own life' rather than as the whole profile every turn.

OPERATOR NOTE for a fresh sync: prompts-sync does not carry promptType or hasStates, so a newly created row lands with promptType=null and will not appear in the main-agent variant picker until it is set to main_agent in prompt management. The placeholder list needs no action — it is parsed from this body automatically.
